neet_phy_u10_t03_2.working: T = 2π√(m/k) does not depend on g, so the period is unchanged on the Moon.

neet_phy_u10_t03_3.working: Each third has k = 3×60 = 180 N/m. Two in parallel give 180 + 180 = 360 N/m.

neet_phy_u10_t03_4.working: Single spring: 2π√(m/k), so A-II. Vertical spring: mg = kΔl, so m/k = Δl/g, giving B-IV. Series: k_eff = k1k2/(k1+k2), giving C-III. Parallel: k_eff = k1+k2, giving D-I.

neet_phy_u10_t03_5.working: A is true: the period is independent of amplitude. B is false: gravity shifts the equilibrium position but not the period. C is false: each part has constant nk. D is true: restoring force constant = ρAg, so T ∝ 1/√ρ. E is true: series k_eff is less than either k. So A, D and E.
